channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average edges up as Trump floats a meeting with Iran
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 51,900 on Monday after its worst week since March. Crude Oil fell back under $100 after President Donald Trump told Fox News he'd probably be open to meeting Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian at the United Nations General Assembly this week.

item.title: British Pound loses grip as Fed hawks stay in charge
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) retreats by some 0.17% on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) trades in the green following last week’s Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike, which widened the interest rate differential between the US and the UK, while still-high energy prices put pressure on major central banks to ra

item.title: BoC’s Macklem: Rate decisions must look beyond initial Oil shock
item.description: Bank of Canada (BoC) Governor Tiff Macklem, speaking in Halifax, Nova Scotia, on Monday, offered a cautious assessment of the economy as higher energy prices and US tariffs create competing risks for inflation and growth.

item.title: WTI Oil extends losing streak as resilient Saudi exports outweigh Middle East risk premium
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil extends its decline for the fourth consecutive day on Monday, trading around $91.90 per barrel at the time of writing, down 3.54% on the day.

item.title: Gold struggles near $4,350 as hawksih Fed outlook supports the Greenback
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains on the defensive on Monday, pausing a two-day winning streak as expectations of additional Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes and a firmer US Dollar (USD) limit the upside.

item.title: Swiss Franc advances after recent sell-off, SNB in focus
item.description: USD/CHF extends its pullback on Monday after climbing to 0.8263 last week, its highest level since May 2025.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk high as 160 seen possible against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that a reported Bank of Japan rate check briefly pushed USD/JPY below 157.0 and suggests authorities may focus on the pace of moves rather than a specific level.

item.title: Japanese Yen slides as Fed hawkishness, intervention fears grow
item.description: USD/JPY extends its advance on Monday and trades around 157.45 at the time of writing, up 0.36% on the day.

item.title: Euro struggles against US Dollar as hawkish Fed outlook weighs
item.description: EUR/USD trades with a downside bias on Monday as the US Dollar holds near recent highs, supported by expectations of additional Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes. Developments in the Middle East also remain in focus.

item.title: Oil: Tightness turning critical – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem argue that global Oil product markets have shifted from tight to critical. They link East-West pipeline disruptions, Russian outages, elevated freight and low inventories to structurally constrained supply.

item.title: United States: Midterm outcomes and policy paths – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) strategist Angelo Katsoras analyzes how the 2026 United States (US) midterm elections could reshape policy under President Trump. He notes Democrats are favoured by high inflation, weak approval ratings and a strong generic ballot lead.

item.title: Euro steadies vs British Pound as German political uncertainty, PMIs cap direction
item.description: EUR/GBP trades around 0.8575 on Monday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day. The Euro (EUR) struggles to regain bullish momentum against the British Pound (GBP), as political concerns in Germany partly offset support from falling Oil prices.

item.title: Indian Rupee: AI imports add pressure against US Dollar – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Anubhuti Sahay and Saurav Anand highlight that India’s AI-enabling goods trade deficit has become the second-largest contributor to the country’s trade gap after Oil, overtaking Gold.

item.title: Gold: CTA whipsaws but support holds – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ commodity strategists report that CTAs (Commodity Trading Advisors) have reversed recent Gold buying, yet emphasize that discretionary investors continue to support the metal.

item.title: Canadian Dollar remains under pressure as hawkish Fed contrasts with steady BoC
item.description: USD/CAD holds firm near the 1.4000 psychological mark on Monday as the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) hawkish outlook and widening US-Canada interest-rate differentials keep the Canadian Dollar (CAD) on the back foot.

item.title: US Dollar: Oil-driven support as Fed seen hiking – ING
item.description: ING strategist Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar remains supported as ING now expects the Fed to deliver one final rate hike in December. Despite near-term upside risks for the Dollar, ING keeps a gradually negative longer-term view and anticipates lower energy prices in Q4.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ hike underwhelms as yields drive JPY against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that the Japanese Yen (JPY) weakened after the BoJ’s 25 bp hike to 1.25% as limited guidance on further normalisation disappointed hawkish expectations.

item.title: Experts agree: Further US Dollar’s upside hinges on upcoming data and not hawkish Fed prospects
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) trades slightly higher on Monday as traders remain confident that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will hike interest rates again this year. At press time, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, trades 0.1% higher to near 100.30.

item.title: Silver price edges up as lower Oil, guarded Fed stance temper upside
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) starts the week on a positive note, gaining 0.37% on Monday to trade around $66.50 at the time of writing. The precious metal manages to advance despite a stable US Dollar (USD), with the US Dollar Index (DXY) trading virtually unchanged around 100.25.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecasts: Bears remain in control with 1.1450 support eyed
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is consolidating last week’s decline against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, with price action capped below 1.1500 and the seven-week low in the mid 1.1400s still on the bears’ radar.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Sideways range against US Dollar intact – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Christian Lawrence and Molly Schwartz expect USD/MXN to trade broadly between 17 and 18 over the next 12 months. They see room for both Fed and Banxico rate expectations to be repriced, with the timing of those adjustments likely to drive near-term volatility.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Momentum stabilizes, but lacks bullish conviction
item.description: GBP/JPY edges higher on Monday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains under pressure across the board in thin trading conditions. Japanese markets are closed until Wednesday for the country’s Silver Week holidays.

item.title: Brent: Diesel signals higher prices – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem highlight a sharp divergence between physical Brent and futures, with Dated Brent trading at a substantial premium. They note that Diesel strength implies Brent should be above $150/bbl to restore historical refining economics.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar wavers near two-month lows despite a brighter market mood
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) languishes just above two-and-a-half-month lows against the US Dollar (USD), despite a somewhat brighter market mood, as a sustained reversal in Oil prices has eased risk aversion on Monday.

item.title: Gold: Range-bound outlook with Fed headwinds – ING
item.description: ING’s commodities team reports Gold eased as markets digest the Federal Reserve’s first rate hike since 2023 and guidance for prolonged restrictive policy. They stress that higher rates remain a headwind, but ETF holdings at six‑month highs and ongoing central bank buying should cushion downside.

item.title: Fed’s Goolsbee: Demand, tariffs, energy, supply shocks all are fuelling inflation
item.description: Chicago Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank President Austan Goolsbee said at an Official Monetary and Financial Institutions Forum event on Monday that various factors including strong demand, tariffs, energy and supply shocks are fuelling United States (US) inflationary pressures.

item.title: Indian Rupeee gains due to further correction in oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) starts the week on a positive note against the US Dollar (USD). The USD/INR pair drops to near 95.75 as the Indian currency gains due to continuous support from correcting oil prices.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges higher on renewed RBA hike bets ahead of Bullock, jobs data
item.description: AUD/USD edges higher on Monday, trading around 0.7130 at the time of writing, up 0.06% on the day. The Australian Dollar (AUD) benefits mainly from strengthening expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) could raise interest rates again at its monetary policy meeting next week.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: Struggles to hold above 20-day EMA
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) is down 0.61% to near $4,350 during the European trading session on Monday. The yellow metal is under pressure as the US Dollar (USD) remains broadly firm amid solid expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will hike interest rates again this year.

item.title: Swiss Franc recovery halts with SNB monetary policy coming into focus
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) nurses minor losses against the US Dollar (USD) to pare some of the previous two trading days’ recovery.
